Laura / team,

Quick triage update:
- Telemetry shows a KV cache prefetch storm in us-west-2a that doubled GPU memory churn around 08:40-08:52 PT; several inference workers went into backpressure and then restarted by the node manager.
- Autoscaler applied scale-up but placement delayed due to fragment allocation constraints (we had two maintenance drains in the same AZ earlier today).
- Fallback routing to us-west-2b was configured, but our routing controller used AZ affinity policy for session stickiness which limited reroute effectiveness for warm sessions.

Immediate mitigation steps taken (in-progress):
1) Forced drain for affected worker pools in us-west-2a (to stop noisy restarts).
2) Tweaked routing policy to prefer cross-AZ failover (reduce affinity window from 20s -> 2s).
3) Triggered burst capacity in us-west-2b (temporary dedicated pool) — provisioning ETA ~18 minutes.

I will continue monitoring and post metrics. If the burst pool can't onboard fast enough, we should consider a cross-region route to us-west-1 as a fallthrough.

Rishi
Staff Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Samir — quick update and commitments:

What happened: our telemetry shows an unexpected KV cache prefetch amplification combined with two maintenance drains that reduced available headroom in us-west-2a. The routing controller honored AZ affinity and did not shift sticky sessions quickly enough, which kept a fraction of traffic on the degraded AZ. That produced a transient 5xx spike and p95 degradation.

Immediate actions were taking:
- Forced drains and route preference change (Rishi) — we expect error rate to drop within 10-20 minutes.
- Brought up a temporary burst pool in us-west-2b; cross-region fallback (us-west-1) is on standby.
- CS will run a post-incident quality check on outputs for sampled requests from the event window.

Customer impact window we see so far: ~08:43 - 09:03 PT (approx 20 minutes). We're preparing a short incident note and a proposed one-time usage credit for the affected window.

Next steps: Hannah will send a customer-friendly incident summary with timeline and mitigations within 90 mins. Samir, if you want an exec bridge, we can open a 30-minute sync — otherwise we'll route updates through you.

Apologies for the disruption — we know checkout is high priority. We'll follow up with a root cause writeup and remediation plan (short term: routing affinity hardening; medium term: avoid maintenance collocation in primary AZ for large accounts).

Laura Bennett
Account Exec — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident summary: NovaCare latency spike (us-west-2) — final note

Jordan / Samir,

Thanks again for the quick flag. Below is the final summary for the event window and next actions.

Timeline (UTC):
- 15:43:12 UTC (08:43 PT): KV cache prefetch amplification begins from warm sessions; memory churn increases.
- 15:48:30 UTC: Node manager triggers restarts on two inference worker nodes in us-west-2a.
- 15:50:20 UTC: Routing controller adjusts affinity window and begins cross-AZ steering.
- 16:03:05 UTC: Burst pool in us-west-2b online and traffic rebalanced; error rate drops to baseline by 16:05 UTC.

Impact: Estimated 20-minute window of elevated errors (peak 7% 5xx) and increased p95 latency. We sampled 1,200 requests from the window and verified model outputs retain expected fidelity; no data leakage observed.

Remediations planned:
- Immediate: route-affinity default hardened, maintenance scheduling checks to avoid same-AZ drains for large customers.
- 2-week: implement a preemptive placement guard that refuses colocated maintenance when headroom < X%.
- 90-day: provide NovaCare an SLA addendum for priority rehoming and a playbook for urgent burst activation.

Credit proposal: one-time credit equivalent to the affected usage for the 20-minute window (proposal sent to finance / legal), pending approval.

Attachments: attached are the log snippet and KPI heatmap showing the spike window.

If you'd like an exec bridge for a quick debrief, Laura can coordinate times.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Reliability Lead — Redwood Inference
